title: Prohibited Trading Strategies
content:
At FundedSquad, we maintain a strict zero-tolerance policy toward any trading behavior designed to exploit demo account environments or bypass fair trading practices. Any strategy that attempts to generate artificial, risk-free, or manipulated profits is strictly forbidden and will result in immediate disqualification.
Examples of Prohibited Strategies Include:
Platform Manipulation
​
Exploiting platform or server issues, such as freezing or glitches in demo environments
Trading on delayed or outdated price feeds or charts not reflecting real-time market data
​
Arbitrage & Latency Exploits
​
Latency arbitrage:
taking advantage of pricing delays between brokers or feeds
Hedge arbitrage:
using multiple accounts to profit from mismatched execution
High-frequency trading (HFT)
and tick scalping via bots or automated systems
​
Risk Manipulation Strategies
​
Martingale strategies:
increasing lot size after a loss to recover prior losses
​
Layering
​
Definition:
Having 3 or more open positions at the same time on a single asset.
This is to prevent excessive exposure and risk buildup on a single trading pair.
​
All Or Nothing
​
Using full margin, unreasonably large lot sizes, or positioning without regard to account size or market conditions
These behaviors reflect unsustainable trading and violate our principles of long-term risk management
For clarification or questions about what constitutes a compliant strategy, please contact our support team before engaging in any questionable activity (
support@fundedsquad.com

title: What is the 1% Max Floating Rule on Instant Rapid?
content:
If a position's floating loss goes past 1% of your account balance, your account breaches immediately.
The
1% Max Floating Rule
is Instant Rapid's single-trade risk control. It caps how much unrealized (floating) loss any one open position can carry before your account is breached.
The rule
If your floating loss on a position exceeds
1% of your account balance
at any point, your account breaches. This is a hard breach with no warning and no grace period, the moment the 1% threshold is crossed, the account is closed.
Example
Account balance: $10,000 — 1% floating loss threshold: $100. If an open position's unrealized loss reaches $100 or more at any point, the account is breached.
Warning
This rule applies to floating (unrealized) loss on open positions, separately from your daily and overall drawdown limits. A trade doesn't need to close for this rule to trigger, crossing the 1% threshold while the position is still open is enough.
[Good to know]
This rule applies on top of the standard per-pair lot size limits — it isn't a replacement for them.

title: Trailing Drawdown (Instant Rapid)
content:
At FundedSquad, protecting your capital while allowing your profits to reduce risk is a key priority. Trailing drawdown is a dynamic loss limit that adjusts as your account makes profits, but
locks at the initial account balance
. Once this lock is reached, the drawdown no longer decreases, even after withdrawals or account resets.
⚙️ How Trailing Drawdown Works on Instant Rapid
Instant Rapid uses a 5% trailing overall drawdown. Every percentage of profit you make is subtracted from your initial 5% drawdown limit, until the drawdown reaches your initial account balance. Once it reaches this level, it locks and no longer adjusts, even after withdrawal or account reset.
📊 Drawdown Parameters

🧮 Example
Let's assume your Instant Rapid Account is $10,000, and the trailing drawdown limit is 5%:
Initial Drawdown

Trade Scenario:
The trader makes a profit of $300 (3% of the account). The trailing drawdown adjusts accordingly:

initial account balance
, it locks.
📉 Daily Drawdown
Instant Rapid also has a separate 3% daily drawdown limit, calculated from your daily opening balance and resetting every day. This is independent of the trailing overall drawdown above.
Example
Account balance: $10,000 — Daily drawdown limit: $300 (3%). If your account drops to $9,700 at any point during the day, your account will be breached and closed.
Single-trade risk rule
Instant Rapid also enforces a 1% Max Floating Rule: if a position's floating (unrealized) loss goes past 1% of your account balance at any point, the account breaches immediately. This is separate from the drawdown limits above and doesn't require the trade to close first.
Warning
Breaching either the daily or overall drawdown limit will result in immediate account termination. Both open floating losses and closed trade losses count toward your drawdown at all times.

Every Funded Retry account includes a 1% floating loss rule. It works in two stages, and getting both stages right matters, since the consequence changes the second time it happens.

First time floating loss exceeds 1%:
your profit split is reduced from 50% to 40%. Your account stays open and active.

title: One Retry Per Account: The Progression Rule
content:
🔁 Overview
Retry gives you exactly one free credit per account, not one per stage. Whichever stage you first fail and claim a retry at, that credit is now used, and it stays used, even as you progress through later stages on a completely different failure than the one that triggered it.
🧭 How Progression Works
Once you claim your account's retry credit at any stage, every stage you pass through afterward runs on
that stage's retry ruleset
, not the original ruleset, because your account is now on the retry track for good.
Retry Paths by Account Type
Account Type
Retry Path
1-Step / 1-Step Pro
Phase 1 Retry → Funded Retry
2-Step Fast / 2-Step Squad
Phase 1 Retry → Phase 2 Retry → Funded Retry
Instant Lite / Instant Pro
Funded Retry (single stage)
🧮 Worked Example: The Edge Case
This is the scenario that catches people out.
A 2-Step trader fails their original
Phase 1
. They claim their free
Phase 1 Retry
— this uses their account's one retry credit.
They pass Phase 1 Retry and advance to
Phase 2
. Because their account is already on the retry track, this Phase 2 attempt runs on
Phase 2 Retry rules
, not the original Phase 2 rules.
They fail this Phase 2 attempt.
Result: no second retry.
Their account's single retry credit was already used at Phase 1. Reaching Phase 2 through the retry track doesn't generate a new, independent credit. To continue, they need to purchase a new account.
✅ The Rule in One Line
Your account gets exactly one free retry, not one per stage. It's used the moment you first claim it, and every stage you reach after that runs on retry rules until you pass all the way through or fail again and need to purchase a new account.

content:
At FundedSquad, we maintain a strict zero-tolerance policy toward any trading behavior designed to exploit demo account environments or bypass fair trading practices. Platform Manipulation
Exploiting platform or server issues, such as freezing or glitches in demo environments
Trading on delayed or outdated price feeds or charts not reflecting real-time market data
Arbitrage & Latency Exploits
Latency arbitrage:
taking advantage of pricing delays between brokers or feeds
Hedge arbitrage:
using multiple accounts to profit from mismatched execution
High-frequency trading (HFT)
and tick scalping via bots or automated systems

Risk Manipulation Strategies

Martingale strategies:
increasing lot size after a loss to recover prior losses
​
Layering
Definition:
Having 3 or more open positions at the same time on a single asset.
This is to prevent excessive exposure and risk buildup on a single trading pair.
​
All Or Nothing
​
Using full margin, unreasonably large lot sizes, or positioning without regard to account size or market conditions
These behaviors reflect unsustainable trading and violate our principles of long-term risk management
​
For clarification or questions about what constitutes a compliant strategy, please contact our support team before engaging in any questionable activity (

title: Position Management Rules
content:
At FundedSquad, we are committed to maintaining a fair, disciplined, and risk-controlled trading environment. As such, the following trading strategies and behaviors are strictly prohibited and may lead to immediate account disqualification:
Hedging
Not allowed
within the same account or across multiple accounts owned by the same or different traders.
​
Definition:
Opening two opposing positions (buy and sell) on the same asset, regardless of lot size.
Martingale Strategy
Definition:
Increasing the lot size after a loss in an attempt to recover previous losses.
This high-risk strategy is a form of stacking and is strictly forbidden.
Layering Rule
Definition:
You are not allowed to have
3 or more open positions
at the same time on a single asset.
This is to prevent excessive exposure and risk buildup on a single trading          pair.
​
One-Sided Betting (All-In Exposure)
Definition: One-sided betting refers to opening trades where the majority or entirety of the account’s available margin is exposed in a single directional bias on one asset or across correlated assets.
This includes using excessively large position sizes or concentrating risk in one direction, resulting in all-in or near all-in exposure.
This behavior is considered high-risk, unsustainable, and is strictly prohibited.
Reminder:
These restrictions are in place to protect the integrity of our platform and ensure that all traders operate under fair and sustainable trading practices. For any questions or clarification regarding allowed strategies, please contact our support team.

title: What is a trading day?
content:
A trading day is any 24-hour period from 8 PM EST to 8 PM EST where you place at least one trade. It is used to track your trading activity and performance during evaluation or funded phases.
A trading day only counts when you meet the required profit condition within that 24-hour cycle.
📅 How does a trading day count?
A trading day is counted when you place at least one trade within the 24-hour period from 8 PM EST to 8 PM EST and achieve a minimum of 0.5% profit based on your initial balance.
This means the trading day will only be valid if you both trade and reach 0.5% profit or more within the same cycle.
❌ What if I don't reach the 0.5% profit target?
If you do not reach at least 0.5% profit within the 24-hour trading day window, then that day will not be counted as a valid trading day.
You can still continue trading on other days until you meet the requirement.
📊 Are there any examples of trading days?
Example
Trade Details
Result
Example 1
You place a trade at 9 PM EST and close it at 7 PM EST with a 0.3% profit.
This does not count as a trading day because the profit is below 0.5%.
Example 2
You open a trade at 10 PM EST and close it at 6 PM EST with a 0.6% profit within the 8 PM EST to 8 PM EST cycle.
This counts as a valid trading day.
Example 3
You place a trade at 8 PM EST and close it at 3 AM EST with a 0.4% profit.
This does not count as a trading day because the profit requirement was not met.
🔁 Do I have to trade consecutively to count trading days?
No, trading days do not need to be consecutive
.
You only need to achieve at least 0.5% or more profit on
any trading day
for a trade day to count.

title: Position Management Rules
content:
At FundedSquad, we are committed to maintaining a fair, disciplined, and risk-controlled trading environment. As such, the following trading strategies and behaviors are strictly prohibited and may lead to immediate account disqualification:
Hedging
Not allowed
within the same account or across multiple accounts owned by the same or different traders.
​
Definition:
Opening two opposing positions (buy and sell) on the same asset, regardless of lot size.
Martingale Strategy
Definition:
Increasing the lot size after a loss in an attempt to recover previous losses.
This high-risk strategy is a form of stacking and is strictly forbidden.
Layering Rule
Definition:
You are not allowed to have
3 or more open positions
at the same time on a single asset.
This is to prevent excessive exposure and risk buildup on a single trading          pair.
​
One-Sided Betting (All-In Exposure)
Definition: One-sided betting refers to opening trades where the majority or entirety of the account’s available margin is exposed in a single directional bias on one asset or across correlated assets.
This includes using excessively large position sizes or concentrating risk in one direction, resulting in all-in or near all-in exposure.
This behavior is considered high-risk, unsustainable, and is strictly prohibited.
Reminder:
These restrictions are in place to protect the integrity of our platform and ensure that all traders operate under fair and sustainable trading practices. For any questions or clarification regarding allowed strategies, please contact our support team.

title: Why Do My MT5 Trade Times Look Different From My Dashboard?
content:
📌 Overview
If you have noticed that the trade times shown on your MT5 terminal do not match the times shown on your Funded Squad dashboard, do not worry. This is completely normal and is not an error or a sync issue. It is simply a difference in how each platform displays time.
Please Note:
This is not a bug or an error. The time difference between MT5 and your dashboard is expected behaviour and has no impact on your account, trades, or evaluations.
⏱️ The Reason
Important:
MT5 displays trade times in UTC+3 while the Funded Squad dashboard displays all trade times in UTC. This creates a consistent 3 hour difference in how trade times appear across both platforms.

❓ Why Do We Use UTC on the Dashboard?
We standardise all trade times to UTC because we support multiple trading platforms including MT5 and MatchTrader. Each platform uses a different local timezone, so normalising everything to UTC ensures consistency and avoids confusion when comparing trades across different platforms.

title: What Is the Reverse Trading Rule on Instant Rapid?
content:
You cannot open an opposite-direction position on the same pair within 15 minutes of a trade closing at TP or SL. Doing so is treated as Reverse Trading, a rule violation.
The rule
If you open a
Buy
position on a pair (e.g. Gold/XAUUSD) and that trade hits either your Take Profit (TP) or Stop Loss (SL), you must not open a
Sell
position on the same pair within the next 15 minutes.
Likewise, if you open a
Sell
position and it closes at TP or SL, you must not open a
Buy
position on the same pair within the next 15 minutes.
Example
10:00 AM
You open a Buy trade on Gold.
10:05 AM
The trade closes at TP or SL.
Until 10:20 AM
You cannot open a Sell trade on Gold.
Violation example
If you open a Sell trade at 10:12 AM (only 7 minutes after the Buy closed), it will be treated as Reverse Trading and may result in a rule violation.

title: Trailing Drawdown
content:
At FundedSquad, protecting your capital while allowing your profits to reduce risk is a key priority. Trailing drawdown is a dynamic loss limit that adjusts as your account makes profits, but
locks at the initial account balance
. Once this lock is reached, the drawdown no longer decreases, even after withdrawals or account resets.
⚙️ How Trailing Drawdown Works
Trailing drawdown refers to the dynamic adjustment of a trader's maximum allowable loss based on the highest equity point reached during trading. The key difference in this model is that every percentage of profit you make is subtracted from your initial drawdown limit, until the drawdown reaches your initial account balance. Once the drawdown reaches this level, it locks and no longer adjusts (even after withdrawal or account reset).
📊 Accounts Using Trailing Drawdown
Account Type
Trailing Drawdown
Instant Lite
6%
🧮 Example
Let's assume your Instant Lite Account is $50,000, and the trailing drawdown limit is 6%:
Initial Drawdown
6% of $50,000 = $3,000
Initial Maximum Drawdown Figure
$50,000 - $3,000 =
$47,000
Trade Scenario:
The trader makes a profit of $1,500 (3% of the account). The trailing drawdown adjusts accordingly:
New Drawdown Limit
Initial Drawdown − Profit % = 6% − 3% =
3%
New Drawdown Amount
3% of $50,000 =
$1,500
New Maximum Drawdown Limit
$50,000 − $1,500 =
$48,500
🔒 Once the drawdown reaches the
initial account balance
, it locks.
Proper management within your trailing drawdown ensures your trading account remains compliant while locking in your profits.
